newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Shorter Malaysia stock settlement seen in 3rd qtr.
newsitem.headline: Shorter Malaysia stock settlement seen in 3rd qtr.

text.p: The Malaysian stock market is expected to move to a shorter stock settlement period by the third quarter of this year, Securities Commission chairman Munir Majid said on Monday.

Asked when the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange would move to T-plus-five from T-plus-seven, meaning five settlement days from the day of the transaction, he said the exchange has said it intends to do that within the third quarter.
Munir was speaking to reporters following a conference on stocks clearing and settlement period.
Asked if the time frame for shorter settlement was feasible, Munir said: "I think so."
Munir said the change to T-plus-five merely moves payment for share transactions two days earlier, as delivery of shares currently already takes place five days after the transaction.
He said a reduction of settlement to T-plus-three was "not on the cards for now", saying in a speech at the conference that "the objective is not T-plus-three in one fell swoop".
The United States and other developed markets operate on T-plus-three or less, and Malaysia's proposed shorter settlement period is partly to bring its market in line with international standards.
Munir said a shorter settlement will promote increased liquidity, reduce risks and improve efficiency in the Kuala Lumpur share market.

But the Kuala Lumpur bourse has intermittently been spooked by rumours of a shorter settlement being implemented soon, with some market participants arguing such a change will dry up activity especially among retail investors and hurt broker profits.
Munir himself commented on the speculation, noting that there was talk last week that margin financing for stock purchases would change as a result of the shorter settlement.
"Margining does not get into the picture," Munir said. "At the end of the day, the extension of margin rests upon commercial assessment of the credit-worthiness of investors by brokers."
He also said that liquidity should increase, not decrease, as a result of the shorter settlement cycle.

Munir said the exchange's Clearing House has been meeting with brokers to explain the changes and will continue to do so. "There will be no surprises, and every detail of implementation is being looked into," he said.
